title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Mock Exam #15

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #15
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A plant with no water for many days will (1 mark)
   A. Grow faster
   B. Make more flowers
   C. Become weak and may die
   D. Get stronger

2. Which of these is a good way to care for plants at school? (1 mark)
   A. Water them when the soil is dry
   B. Throw litter on them
   C. Pick all the flowers
   D. Trample on flower beds

3. Which of these do animals breathe in from the air? (1 mark)
   A. Water
   B. Dust
   C. Smoke
   D. Oxygen

4. What is the correct order of parts food passes through? (1 mark)
   A. Stomach, mouth, gullet, small intestine
   B. Gullet, mouth, small intestine, stomach
   C. Mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine
   D. Mouth, stomach, gullet, anus

5. Why should you wear shoes and wash hands to prevent worms? (1 mark)
   A. Water makes worms grow
   B. Worms live in shoes
   C. Shoes make food digest
   D. Worm eggs are found in dirty soil and on dirty hands

6. Which of these parts is found after the stomach? (1 mark)
   A. Small intestine
   B. Tongue
   C. Mouth
   D. Gullet

7. How often should teeth be brushed? (1 mark)
   A. Once a year
   B. Never
   C. Once a month
   D. At least twice a day

8. Which of these leaves the body through the anus? (1 mark)
   A. Saliva
   B. Faeces
   C. Blood
   D. Stomach juice

9. Which of these is a danger of solid waste? (1 mark)
   A. It blocks drains and causes floods
   B. It makes air fresh
   C. It grows food
   D. It cleans rivers

10. What does reduce mean? (1 mark)
   A. Burn waste
   B. Use again
   C. Make into new items
   D. Make less waste

11. Why is polythene dangerous for goats and cows? (1 mark)
   A. They may eat it and get sick
   B. It makes milk
   C. It makes them grow
   D. It makes them sweet

12. Which of these is a tool for picking up waste safely? (1 mark)
   A. Bare feet
   B. A rake
   C. Bare hands
   D. A towel

13. What should you do after handling waste? (1 mark)
   A. Wash hands with soap and clean water
   B. Wipe hands on your clothes
   C. Eat at once
   D. Touch your face

14. Which of these is a way of protecting water sources? (1 mark)
   A. Letting animals dirty the spring
   B. Washing clothes in the river
   C. Throwing waste in the river
   D. Planting trees near rivers

15. Which of these helps farmers to save water? (1 mark)
   A. Leaving canals leaking
   B. Drip irrigation
   C. Watering at noon
   D. Flooding the field

16. What is a good message for a water conservation poster? (1 mark)
   A. Water is free for all to waste
   B. Leave the tap open
   C. Close the tap after use
   D. Waste is fun

17. Why should you keep drinking water in a clean covered container? (1 mark)
   A. To keep it safe from germs
   B. To make it colder
   C. To make it hot
   D. To make it salty

18. Which of these describes recycling water? (1 mark)
   A. Cleaning used water so it can be used again
   B. Letting water evaporate
   C. Wasting water
   D. Boiling it and throwing it

19. Which of these shows that friction produces heat? (1 mark)
   A. Drawing with chalk
   B. Rubbing hands together
   C. Pouring water
   D. Looking at a torch

20. Why do we put oil on machine parts? (1 mark)
   A. To make them heavy
   B. To increase friction
   C. To reduce friction
   D. To make them weak

21. Which of these holds objects together? (1 mark)
   A. Glue
   B. A smooth floor
   C. A rolling ball
   D. Oil

22. Which force is at work when you pour water and it flows down a slope? (1 mark)
   A. Light
   B. Magnetism only
   C. Gravity
   D. Sound

23. Which is a use of gravity? (1 mark)
   A. Making objects float in air
   B. Water flowing downhill
   C. Lifting up a stone by itself
   D. Making air hot

24. A force can be small or big. A bigger push makes a ball go (1 mark)
   A. Change colour
   B. Faster and further
   C. Not move
   D. Slower

25. What does a red traffic light tell a driver? (1 mark)
   A. Stop
   B. Speed up
   C. Go
   D. Turn on lights

26. What is a source of light? (1 mark)
   A. Something that is dark
   B. Something that blocks light
   C. Something that gives out its own light
   D. Something that reflects light

27. Which of these is a safety use of light? (1 mark)
   A. Making shadows
   B. Making sound
   C. Street lights
   D. Colouring paint

28. What do solar panels change sunlight into? (1 mark)
   A. Food
   B. Sound
   C. Water
   D. Electricity

29. Which project helps you to handle hot pots safely? (1 mark)
   A. Making kitchen gloves
   B. Making a toy
   C. Making a dustbin
   D. Making a poster

30. What should you use to hold a hot cooking pot? (1 mark)
   A. A plastic bag
   B. Kitchen gloves or a thick dry cloth
   C. Bare hands
   D. Wet cloth

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Describe how you would organise the cleaning of a school compound using safe methods. (5 marks)

32. Give two symptoms of an unhealthy digestive system. (2 marks)

33. Why is used washing water not safe for drinking? Give one good way to use it. (3 marks)

34. Describe how you would make a dustbin from locally available materials. (4 marks)

35. A pupil grows two bean seedlings. One is put in a cupboard and the other in the sunlight. Both are watered. After a week the two look different. Describe what she might see and give a reason. (4 marks)

36. A block is pulled along a rough floor and along a smooth floor with the same force. Describe and explain what you would see. (4 marks)

37. Describe how you would do an activity to show gravity. (4 marks)

38. Give three ways of protecting water sources. (3 marks)

39. Describe what happens in the small intestine and why it is important. (4 marks)

40. Describe how a pupil can tell that an earthworm is an animal. (3 marks)

41. Name the three main sources of heat. (2 marks)

42. Explain the difference between reusing and recycling. (3 marks)

43. Describe three examples each of reducing and reusing water. (4 marks)

44. Name the two forces studied in this topic. (2 marks)

45. What should you do for a small burn? State three actions. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #15 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Become weak and may die
   Water is needed for life, so a plant without it wilts and may die.

2. A — Water them when the soil is dry
   Watering when dry helps plants live and grow.

3. D — Oxygen
   Animals need oxygen from the air or water.

4. C — Mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine
   Food goes from the mouth down the gullet to the stomach and then the small intestine.

5. D — Worm eggs are found in dirty soil and on dirty hands
   Worm eggs can enter the body through dirt.

6. A — Small intestine
   Food moves from the stomach to the small intestine.

7. D — At least twice a day
   Brushing morning and night keeps teeth healthy.

8. B — Faeces
   Faeces leave the body through the anus.

9. A — It blocks drains and causes floods
   Waste blocks drains and water floods the area.

10. D — Make less waste
   To reduce is to make less waste.

11. A — They may eat it and get sick
   Animals that eat polythene can become ill or die.

12. B — A rake
   A rake or shovel keeps hands away from the waste.

13. A — Wash hands with soap and clean water
   Washing removes germs.

14. D — Planting trees near rivers
   Tree roots hold the soil and protect water.

15. B — Drip irrigation
   Drip irrigation gives water directly to roots.

16. C — Close the tap after use
   A short, clear message helps people remember.

17. A — To keep it safe from germs
   Covered clean containers protect water.

18. A — Cleaning used water so it can be used again
   Recycling cleans water for another use.

19. B — Rubbing hands together
   Rubbing surfaces produces heat.

20. C — To reduce friction
   Oil makes surfaces slide easily.

21. A — Glue
   Glue, nails and ropes use forces to hold things together.

22. C — Gravity
   Gravity pulls water downhill.

23. B — Water flowing downhill
   Gravity makes water flow downhill.

24. B — Faster and further
   A stronger force has a bigger effect.

25. A — Stop
   Red means stop.

26. C — Something that gives out its own light
   A source of light makes its own light.

27. C — Street lights
   Street lights help people see at night.

28. D — Electricity
   Solar panels make electricity from sunlight.

29. A — Making kitchen gloves
   Gloves protect hands.

30. B — Kitchen gloves or a thick dry cloth
   Gloves stop heat reaching your hand.

SECTION B
----
31. (5 marks)
   Answer: Form groups with roles. Wear gloves and shoes. Use rakes and shovels. Sort waste into decomposable and non-decomposable bins. Take compost to the pit. Wash hands after.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step up to 5.

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: Stomach ache, bloating, diarrhoea, vomiting, constipation, worms (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: It has dirt and germs. It can be used to water plants or mop floors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for dirty water, 1 mark for germs, 1 mark for a safe use.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a strong bucket, box or container. Cut and smooth the top and cover any sharp edge. Make a lid if possible. Paint a label saying waste only and put it in a suitable place.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: The plant in the cupboard looks weak and pale and the one in the light is green and healthy. Plants need light to make food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for describing each plant and 2 marks for the reason.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: The block moves slower or a shorter distance on the rough floor. Rough floors give more friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Drop a stone and a ball from the same height. Observe that they fall down to the ground. Gravity pulls them down.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for items, 1 mark for dropping, 1 mark for observing downward fall, 1 mark for conclusion.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plant trees near rivers, do not throw waste in water, do not wash in springs, keep animals away from drinking sources.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

39. (4 marks)
   Answer: Digestion is finished there. Digested food passes through the wall into the blood. The blood carries it to all parts of the body for energy, growth and repair.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point up to 4.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: It feeds on soil, grows, breathes, moves, responds to touch, reproduces and removes waste. It shows the signs of life.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct sign, up to 3.

41. (2 marks)
   Answer: The sun, fire and electricity.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two and 2 marks for all three.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Reusing means using an item again in the same or a new way without changing it, for example a bottle for water. Recycling means turning waste into a new product, for example melting old plastic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for reuse, 1 mark for recycle, 1 mark for one example.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Reduce: close taps, fix leaks, use a cup. Reuse: washing vegetables water on plants, laundry water for mopping, rainwater for the garden.
   Working / marking points: Award marks for correct examples up to a total of 4.

44. (2 marks)
   Answer: Gravity and friction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put it under cool running water, cover with a clean cloth, tell an adult and do not put butter or oil.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.
